profiles.name: Brian Hynes
profiles.description: Brian Hynes is a Bronx peace activist associated with Upstate Drone Action. On October 25, 2012, he joined a nonviolent blockade at Hancock Field Air National Guard Base near Syracuse, New York, where activists tried to deliver a citizens’ indictment protesting U.S. drone warfare. A DeWitt Town Court judge found Hynes guilty of disorderly conduct, acquitted him of trespass, and on February 7, 2014 imposed a 15-day jail sentence, a fine, and a two-year order barring him from Hancock Field.
profiles.finding: Veterans for Peace Hancock article names Hynes in group action; no individually identified portrait verified. Winona football namesake rejected.

profiles.name: Daniel Burgevin
profiles.description: Daniel Burgevin is a peace activist from Trumansburg, New York and participant in Upstate Drone Action. On October 1, 2012, he was among a group of activists who entered Hancock Field Air National Guard Base near Syracuse to protest the U.S. drone warfare program. Hancock trains drone pilots and coordinates lethal MQ-9 Reaper drone strikes in Afghanistan. Burgevin was convicted of disorderly conduct and sentenced to 15 days in Onondaga County Jail in 2013.
profiles.finding: Peace Council action coverage identifies Dan Burgevin and credits group photo to Heriberto Rodriguez; individual portrait remains unverified.

profiles.name: Mark Scibilia-Carver
profiles.description: Mark Scibilia-Carver is a peace activist from Trumansburg, New York who participated in the October 2012 protest at Hancock Field Air National Guard Base near Syracuse, where activists trespassed to protest the U.S. drone warfare program. Hancock trains pilots for MQ-9 Reaper drones that carry out lethal strikes in Afghanistan and other countries. Scibilia-Carver was convicted of disorderly conduct and sentenced to 15 days in Onondaga County Jail in 2013.
profiles.finding: Peace Council and Nuclear Resister action coverage corroborates identity; group/photo lead needs subject identification. No portrait added.

profiles.name: Pratheepan Thavaraja
profiles.description:
Pratheepan Thavaraja, Nachimuthu Socrates, Murugesu Vinayagamoorthy, Vijayshanthar Patpanathan, Gaspar Raj Maria Paulian, Namasivaya Viswanathan, and an unknown individual conspired to provide resources, currency, training, and false documents to the Tamil Tigers. Paulian met with a prospective financial contributor to discuss bribing a State Department official to remove the Tamil Tigers from the U.S. government’s list of foreign terrorist organizations. Socrates wrote a $500 check to an informant posing as a State Department official and then gave $5,000 to another person he believed was also a State Department official. In addition, Socrates relayed to a Tamil Tigers member the contents of what he believed was a classified document purchased from State Department officials.

Case characteristics: FBI sting operation, FBI confidential informant. Organization referenced in charging documents: Tamil Tigers.

Case data and description from The Intercept's Trial and Terror project (Trevor Aaronson and Margot Williams), licensed CC BY-NC. Source: https://github.com/theintercept/trial-and-terror-data
profiles.finding: Federal appellate decision corroborates LTTE defendant; Sri Lankan graduate listing is not linked to defendant and rejected.

profiles.name: Raynaldo Rivera
profiles.description: Raynaldo Rivera, known online as neuron, royal and wildicv, was a member of LulzSec, an offshoot the Justice Department described as affiliated with Anonymous. He surrendered to the FBI in Phoenix in August 2012 and pleaded guilty for his role in the 2011 intrusion into Sony Pictures. On August 8, 2013 he was sentenced to a year and a day in federal prison, thirteen months of home detention, 1,000 hours of community service and restitution. Whether he remained continuously detained after surrendering is not established in the public record, so his prison-entry date is left blank.
profiles.finding: San Antonio Current interview corroborates defendant. Image caption describes programming awards rather than portrait; linked image retrieval failed. Author avatar rejected.

profiles.name: Nathan Walker Joseph
profiles.description: Nathan Walker Joseph, known as Ducky, is an environmental activist who joined Mountain Justice and RAMPS organizers in a May 24, 2012 protest against mountaintop-removal coal mining. Joseph and four other activists boarded and locked themselves to a coal barge at the Quincy Docks near Chelyan, West Virginia, while a related group blocked a mine haul road on Kayford Mountain. Joseph later pleaded guilty to obstruction, entered South Central Regional Jail on August 30 to serve a five-day sentence, and was released September 3 after just over 96 hours.
profiles.finding: Exact name and Ducky/Quincy coal-barge refinements produced no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Christopher French
profiles.description: Christopher French, an anti-NATO protester from Beaver Dam, Wisconsin, was arrested in Chicago on May 20, 2012 after a confrontation near Van Buren Street and Wabash Avenue during protests surrounding the NATO summit. Prosecutors initially charged him with felony aggravated battery of police officers. French spent 84 days in jail before posting bond. On August 15, 2013, he pleaded guilty to misdemeanor resisting arrest after prosecutors dropped the felony charge. Judge Carol Howard sentenced him to 364 days in Cook County Jail, credited the 84 days already served, and imposed $254 in fines and fees.
profiles.finding: Storming Heaven newsletter corroborates NATO case; military, musician and psychologist namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Raziel Azuara
profiles.description: Raziel Azuara was arrested during protests against the NATO summit in Chicago on May 20, 2012. Police accused him of throwing a light bulb filled with red paint toward officers near Cermak Road and Michigan Avenue. He was initially charged with aggravated battery to a police officer and held on $150,000 bail. In March 2014, shortly after the NATO 3 trial, Azuara pleaded guilty to misdemeanor battery and received two years of probation and 20 hours of community service.
profiles.finding: CBS NATO vigil coverage and Nuclear Resister newsletter corroborate case; no identifiable individual portrait verified.

profiles.name: Yonte Harris
profiles.description: Yonte Harris was arrested during protests against the NATO summit in Chicago on May 20, 2012. Police alleged that Harris grabbed an officer’s legs during a confrontation and pushed the officer’s bicycle into the officer’s chest. Harris was charged with aggravated battery to a police officer and ordered held on $200,000 bail. Contemporary prisoner-support reports continued to list him in Cook County Jail after the summit; the available sources do not establish his exact release date or the final disposition of the charge.
profiles.finding: CBS/ABC NATO reporting corroborates case; no identifiable individual portrait verified.

profiles.name: Cody Ingram
profiles.description: Cody Ingram was charged in federal court (W.D. Wash.) with destruction of government property after the Occupy Seattle May Day 2012 march, in which a black-bloc faction smashed glass doors at the William Kenzo Nakamura U.S. Courthouse on 5th Avenue with a wooden stick. According to Seattle Times reporting, Ingram is the only federally-prosecuted defendant from the May Day 2012 march to actually serve federal time — described in subsequent press accounts as "just over a month in prison" for damage to the courthouse doors.
profiles.finding: SeattlePI sentencing coverage corroborates May Day case; Alabama university photographer not linked and rejected.

profiles.name: Joshua Wollstein
profiles.description: Joshua Wollstein, then 28 and from Tacoma, Washington, was charged with riot — a Class C felony under Washington state law — for his role in the May Day 2012 Occupy Seattle march that broke off into a black-bloc property-damage rampage downtown. Prosecutors said Wollstein threw two beer bottles at Seattle Police Department officers at 5th and Olive, struck a detective in the shin while resisting arrest, and was carrying a lead-loaded leather sap. Of the eight arrested in connection with the May Day march where prosecutors' charges held up, Wollstein is the most prominently identified state-court defendant; he served roughly two months at the King County Jail in 2012-2013.
profiles.finding: Seattle Weekly identity-specific interview is a promising portrait lead but source failed retrieval twice; follow-up pending.

profiles.name: Ernesto Wilson
profiles.description: Charged as an *associate* (not a formal member) of the Greensboro chapter of the Almighty Latin King & Queen Nation. Indicted December 2011 and convicted at trial November 21, 2012 on federal RICO conspiracy and VICAR charges. Sentenced August 13, 2013 to 17 years in federal prison.
profiles.finding: Federal appellate decision corroborates Greensboro case; model result not linked to defendant and rejected.

profiles.name: Cameron Rose
profiles.description: Cameron Rose was arrested about a month after a December 2011 confrontation at an Occupy Oakland teepee vigil outside Oakland City Hall, in which he was accused of striking a police officer with a folding chair. Taken into custody on January 22, 2012, he was held in pretrial detention because he could not post the unusually high 130,000-dollar bond. A jury convicted him of resisting an executive officer and misdemeanor assault on a peace officer while acquitting him of felony assault with a deadly weapon; the judge suspended imposition of a prison sentence and placed him on five years probation, with no additional jail. His exact release date is not publicly confirmed; he was released upon that disposition. His case is better understood as pretrial political detention than a prison sentence.
profiles.finding: KQED, SFGate and Occupy Oakland trial reporting are relevant leads; no individual portrait verified. Unrelated directory and social results rejected.
